_source: BPHS = Brihat Parasara Hora Sastra, tr. R. Santhanam, Vol. 1 (Ranjan Publications, New Delhi), Ch 34 'Yoga Karakas' (printed pp. 341-349), Ch 3 'Planetary characters', Ch 6-7 (divisional charts), Ch 27 'Evaluation of strengths', Ch 44 'Maraka (killer) planets'. Phaladeepika = Phaladeepika of Mantreswara, tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950, Adhyaya 20 'Dasas of the several bhava lords and their bhuktis'. Every verse number below was read in the archive.org full text of these editions; where only a chapter is given, the verse was not checked.

natural.note: Phase 1: Mercury is treated as a benefic (BPHS Ch 34 vv. 8-10: Mercury takes the nature of his associates and is favourable when alone; association is not evaluated yet). The Moon is a benefic when waxing (shukla paksha) and a malefic when waning.

lagna_lord.text: The lagna lord is specially auspicious, since the lagna is both a kendra and a trikona; it stays benefic even when it also owns an evil house.
lagna_lord.ref: BPHS Ch 34 vv. 2-7; Phaladeepika Ch 20 v. 41

yogakaraka.text: Owning a kendra and a trikona together makes a planet a yogakaraka.

trikona_lord.text: The lord of a trikona (5th or 9th) gives auspicious results, even when it also owns the 8th or another evil house.
trikona_lord.ref: BPHS Ch 34 vv. 2-7; Phaladeepika Ch 20 v. 41

dusthana_3_6_11.text: The lord of the 3rd, 6th or 11th gives evil effects.
dusthana_3_6_11.ref: BPHS Ch 34 vv. 2-7; Phaladeepika Ch 20 v. 41

eighth_lord.text: The 8th lord is not auspicious, as the 8th is the 12th from the 9th.
eighth_lord.ref: BPHS Ch 34 vv. 2-7; Phaladeepika Ch 20 v. 41

eighth_lord_luminary.text: The 8th lordship of the Sun or the Moon is not evil; with no other lordship the luminary is neutral.
eighth_lord_luminary.ref: BPHS Ch 34 vv. 2-7; Phaladeepika Ch 20 v. 41

kendradhipati_dosha.text: A natural benefic owning a kendra does not give benefic effects (kendradhipati dosha) and is neutral.

malefic_kendra.text: A natural malefic owning a kendra is not inauspicious; without a trikona it is neutral, not benefic.

lord_2_12.text: The lords of the 2nd and 12th act according to their association; by lordship alone they are neutral.

maraka.text: The 2nd and 7th are the maraka (death-inflicting) houses; their lords carry the maraka role in addition to their other nature.
maraka.ref: BPHS Ch 44; BPHS Ch 34 vv. 19-22; Phaladeepika Ch 20 v. 40

node.text: Rahu and Ketu own no sign for this purpose and are neutral by lordship.
node.node_note: Rahu and Ketu give results according to the house they occupy and the lords they join; in a kendra related to a trikona lord, or in a trikona related to a kendra lord, a node becomes a yogakaraka (BPHS Ch 34 v. 17). This relation is not evaluated yet.

dignity.text: Dignity of the planet in the rashi chart.

shadbala.text: Shadbala against the required minimum (ratio of at least 1 is strong).

combust.text: A combust planet acts like a debilitated one.

house.text: Placement in a kendra or trikona strengthens a planet; placement in the 6th, 8th or 12th weakens it.
house.ref: BPHS Ch 34 v. 13; Phaladeepika Ch 20 vv. 22, 27

vargottama.text: A vargottama planet (same sign in D1 and D9) gives favourable results in its dasha.

d9_dignity.text: Dignity of the planet by sign in the navamsa (D9).

role.text: The dasha lord gives results according to its functional nature for this lagna.

strength.text: A stronger dasha lord gives its results more fully.

rules.text: The dasha lord activates the houses it owns.

occupies.text: The dasha lord activates the house it occupies.

mutual_dusthana.text: The sub-period lord stands 6/8 or 2/12 from the period lord; the 6th, 8th and 12th from the dasha lord give unhappy results.

mutual_kendra_trikona.text: The sub-period lord stands in a kendra or trikona from the period lord; the two lords co-operate.
